reason: Attack failed. This is a translated line, so I went at the translator. Wikisource carries An Account of My Hut from a scan of Keene’s Anthology of Japanese Literature, credits the translation to Donald Keene, and opens: “The flow of the river is ceaseless and its water is never the same. The bubbles that float in the pools, now vanishing, now forming, are not of long duration: so in the world are man and his dwellings”. The proposed sentence is Keene’s first sentence exactly, ending in a full stop, so there is no drift between the wording and the named translation. Keene’s version of the Hōjōki is the one printed in the Anthology of Japanese Literature (Grove Press, 1955), so the edition and year are right, and “the opening sentence” is right. shipped.js: not shipped, no near match, Kamo no Chōmei at 0 of 3, not banned. He is not in personsUsed, so no clash with Sei Shōnagon, Yoshida Kenkō or Dōgen, who are separate people. Essay is the form of the work: the Hōjōki is a prose zuihitsu, not scripture and not liturgy, so the Library rule does not reach it. Source line is 120 characters, leads with the name, no dash, no straight double quote. Pre-1999 by any measure (composed 1212, translated 1955) and entirely publishable. One suggestion, not a refutation: the source could carry the composition year, since the only date it shows is 1955. The citation as written is sound.
